item.title: Far-left ESPN writer mocks Caitlin Clark for losing in the WNBA playoffs, says it proves she isn't a top gurad
item.description: ESPN race writer David Dennis Jr. openly celebrated Caitlin Clark's WNBA playoff elimination, posting a smiling photo and calling her overrated.
item.content:encoded:
An ESPN writer openly celebrated Caitlin Clark's elimination from the WNBA playoffs on Friday by posting a smiling photo of himself on X.

David Dennis Jr. then posted a lengthy thread mocking Clark as overrated. Dennis referenced his previous argument that Clark is "not a top four guard" in the WNBA and claimed this postseason proved him right.

"But let the record reflect that I was 100% right here as well. Because yes we did talk about winning and my concerns about her game translating to winning," Dennis wrote.

He then gloated over Clark losing in the first round.

"A team with 3 top 10 players, according to ESPN, who was a game away from the Finals w/o their star player and then getting bounced in the first round w/ said player is a reason to ask questions. It always is."

ESPN'S COVERAGE OF CAITLIN CLARK IS A RACIALLY CHARGED, DISHONEST, AND EMBARRASSING MESS | BOBBY BURACK

For context, the Fever lost to the Las Vegas Aces, the heavy betting favorites to win their fourth championship in five years. Framing that as Clark getting "bounced in the first round" is intentionally more dismissive than descriptive.

Clark also played well. She became the first player in WNBA history to score 25+ and 15 assists in any game. She is not the reason the Fever lost to a superior team.

Those unfamiliar with Dennis might reasonably wonder why an employee of ESPN, the WNBA Finals rights holder, would celebrate the elimination of the league's biggest television draw. Imagine an NBC personality gloating over the Chiefs' or Cowboys' playoff exit in a season in which NBC broadcasts the Super Bowl.

We can explain.

David Dennis Jr. is a hack. This is the same commentator who last year called for Caitlin Clark fans — who represent a significant portion of the WNBA's audience — to stop watching the league.

ESPN hired Dennis in 2021, promoting that it had "hired the son of a civil rights leader." His addition was part of the network's post-George Floyd hiring push, during which ESPN publicly emphasized race and representation in its talent strategy.

ESPN WRITER WHO BLAMED RACISM FOR HIS ARREST SAYS RACISM IS NOT TO BLAME FOR CAITLIN CLARK HATE

Dennis is a DEI hire, by definition.

And he tries far too hard.

Last year, he posted a rant on Bluesky claiming Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle jeans advertisement "mortified" him because he believed it promoted eugenics.

Dennis seems to have an issue with successful White women, whether it's Clark, Sweeney, or Sophie Cunningham. He is running the same playbook that Jemele Hill, Bomani Jones, and Ryan Clark used before him.

Clark's firing, followed by his unfounded accusations of racism against the network, will likely keep Dennis employed for a few more years. But he's drifting into the sort of territory where only Dan Le Batard would offer him a job.

Speaking of Le Batard, one of his employees, Jessica Smetana, also celebrated the Fever's loss. She compared watching Sophie Cunningham play basketball to serving a sentence at Shawshank.

Like Dennis, Smetana comes across as so bitter. She is probably jealous of Cunningham, as well.

And yet, these same commentators who proudly belittle Clark and Cunningham continue to claim that Black lesbian women are the ones the sports media relentlessly targets.

It's all such a lie.

item.title: Harvard Medical School artist-in-residence calls to ‘Free Luigi’ Mangione during ‘fat liberation’ panel
item.description: Roxane Gay said "Free Luigi" at a Harvard Medical School event before admitting she uses concierge medicine to avoid ordinary healthcare costs.
item.content:encoded:
Roxane Gay, Rutgers University professor artist-in-residence for Harvard's Master of Science in Media, Medicine and Health and Media and Medicine Certificiate Program at Harvard Medical School, called for the release of Luigi Mangione, who pleaded guilty in August to federal stalking charges resulting in death in connection with the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, during a Harvard panel Wednesday examining fatness and healthcare.

When the discussion turned to the health insurance industry, Gay responded, "Free Luigi, for one," and then Gay went on to call the health insurance industry "equal opportunity evil," The College Fix reported.

In a Wednesday post on X from Stu Smith, an investigative analyst at the Manhattan Institute, Smith wrote, "At tonight’s Harvard Medical School event, artist-in-residence Roxane Gay responded to a question about the health insurance industry with ‘Free Luigi.’"

HASAN PIKER SPARKS BACKLASH WITH LUIGI MANGIONE REMARKS, CLAIMS SLAIN CEO ENGAGED IN 'SOCIAL MURDER'

Smith continued, "Minutes earlier, Gay admitted she uses concierge medicine after deciding to ‘throw money at this problem’ and ‘buy my way out’ of ordinary healthcare. Gay, incidentally, is former Harvard president Claudine Gay’s first cousin. We all know Harvard is morally bankrupt at this point, but this was a great reminder."

Gay made the remarks during the Harvard Medical School's "Against the Pathology of Unruly Bodies" event, which focused on what organizers described as the "intersection of fatness and healthcare" and how medical professionals treat overweight patients.

The event also examined, according to a listing advertising the event, "the way fat bodies are pathologized by medical professionals with grave consequences, and how medical professionals can more ethically treat fat patients as people rather than as problems to be solved."

Gay holds the Gloria Steinem Endowed Chair in Media, Culture and Feminist Studies at Rutgers. 

LUIGI MANGIONE PLEADS GUILTY IN FEDERAL COURT TO STALKING AND KILLING UNITEDHEALTHCARE CEO BRIAN THOMPSON

Mangione, who faces a second-degree murder charge, several weapons charges and a forged-instrument charge in New York state court, pleaded guilty Aug. 14 to two federal stalking charges resulting in death. He is scheduled to be sentenced in federal court Dec. 18 and faces a maximum potential sentence of life in prison. His state case remains pending.

LUIGI MANGIONE MUSICAL SET TO MAKE NEW YORK CITY DEBUT IN THE SUMMER

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Gay said, "I said Free Luigi out of utter frustration, and this is a frustration most Americans have about the health insurance industry. That industry is far more focused on profit than actually providing people with the healthcare they need, healthcare that should be covered by the health insurance we pay quite a lot of money for."

Gay continued, "Luigi Mangione was clearly dealing with mental health issues when he committed murder. Murder is wrong, in all cases, including the death penalty. I don't think his mental health issues will be addressed in a carceral setting. He should be in a setting where he can get actual help, not in a place that might exacerbate the mental illness that drove him to commit murder. Unfortunately, our justice system doesn't really care about rehabilitation, so I doubt he will get the help he needs. Whatever his sentence ends up being, I hope he is able to get the help he needs while pays his debt to society and I hope Brian Thompson's family feels justice is served even though nothing will bring back their loved one."

"I condemn the killing of Brian Thompson," Gay said further. "I condemn all killing. Murder doesn't solve anything. Thompson's murder didn't improve the health insurance system. It only created a cavern of grief for his loved ones. You know that. The health insurance industry is absolutely equal opportunity evil. Millions and millions of Americans feel this way. It is not a unique sentiment. I would love for the American health insurance system to evolve into a single payer system so we have universal healthcare like a significant percentage of the rest of the world. At the very, very least, it would be great if health insurance companies didn't make healthcare decisions for patients that should be made by their physicians."

Gay added that "these types of articles result in my receiving death threats and harassment, because they are decontextualized."

A Harvard University spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement, "For the 2026-2027 academic year, Roxane Gay is an artist-in-residence for the Master of Science in Media, Medicine and Health and the Media and Medicine Certificate Program at Harvard Medical School. The views expressed by speakers at events are their own and do not represent Harvard Medical School or Harvard University."

Fox News Digital reached out to Rutgers University for comment.

item.title: Tony Romo and CBS part ways but history suggests former NFL QB will add to his career comeback mark
item.description: Tony Romo's CBS Sports exit after his OWI arrest and plea deal may cost him tens of millions, but history suggests a broadcast booth comeback.
item.content:encoded:
Tony Romo and CBS Sports have mutually agreed to part ways, which was expected following the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback's OWI arrest and plea deal in July and September.

But history suggests Romo will eventually be able to do in the broadcast booth what he did 25 times with the Cowboys: author a comeback.

That assumes he wants to do that, which seems likely.

JIM NANTZ SPEAKS OUT ON 'GREAT FRIEND' TONY ROMO'S OWI ARREST, SAYS HE WILL 'ALWAYS' BE THERE FOR HIM

First the news announced by both CBS Sports and Romo in separate statements:

"CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways," CBS said in a statement on Friday. "We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward.

"J.J. Watt will continue to partner with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on our lead NFL announce team for the rest of the season."

Said Romo in his own statement:

"I’m proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years. I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life – with a desire to win and be the best that I can be.

"I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans."

This needs some context. Romo and CBS negotiated this separation and a source said there was an agreement that includes payments to Romo. The source declined to be specific on the amount that Romo will receive.

Romo signed a 10-year contract in 2020 worth a reported $180 million. He had four years, including this one, remaining on the deal. The remaining portion of that was worth approximately $70-$75 million.

So Romo's Wisconsin intoxication folly almost definitely cost him a lot of money. But the obvious misstep doesn't need to be thought of as a permanent misstep, if Romo indeed gets himself sorted and wants to return to an NFL analyst chair.

He is unquestionably better than the lower-tier game and pregame analysts currently employed by the networks and streaming services. He's also a bigger name who, oddly, gains more attention because of his arrest.

So, it is quite possible that after some time away, Romo will be able to return in one of those roles. And there is precedent for such a return because Romo is not the first flawed NFL analyst who faced legal troubles and worked again.

AL MICHAELS GLOSSES OVER DESHAUN WATSON'S TWO DOZEN SEXUAL MISCONDUCT LAWSUITS, CALLS THEM A 'THING'

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The point is sports television is generally forgiving because the audience is likewise forgiving.

Romo, 46, is currently without driving privileges, which were revoked for six months, he must complete an alcohol-assessment program, install an ignition-interlock device, and he's already paid court costs and fees.

Eventually, TV may be comfortable with believing he has also paid the debt for his crime and welcome him back.
